what_was_done: Loaded raw facility file (KY + 7 border states)
why: Starting point. 128 columns, one row per hospital per week.

what_was_done: Checked duplicate hospital-week rows (kept the corrected row if any)
why: Each hospital should appear once per week.

what_was_done: Replaced the HHS suppression code -999999 with missing
why: HHS uses -999999 for small counts it suppressed. Left as a number it would crush every average. Other negative values after this step: 0.

what_was_done: Kept Short Term and Critical Access hospitals; dropped Long Term and Children's hospitals
why: Adult ICU and general inpatient capacity is not comparable for long-term or children's hospitals. Raw mix: {'Short Term': 132042, 'Critical Access Hospitals': 47723, 'Long Term': 13272, 'Childrens Hospitals': 3832}

what_was_done: Set a measure to missing when the hospital reported it on fewer than 4 of the 7 days
why: A 7-day average built from 1 to 3 days is a weak estimate. Rule: need at least 4 reporting days.

what_was_done: Parsed latitude and longitude from the geocoded address
why: Needed for the Lexington-side / Louisville-side rule. Rows without a geocode keep no region.

what_was_done: Computed occupancy = beds used / beds staffed. Zero-bed denominators left missing; occupancy above 150% set to missing
why: Over 100% can be real (surge beds), so values from 100% to 150% are kept and flagged (1120 rows were above 100% before the 150% cut). Above 150% is treated as a reporting error. Zero-bed denominators: 40583 rows.

what_was_done: Flagged outliers three ways: isolated one-week occupancy spikes, one-off bed-count blips, and occupancy above 100%
why: Isolated spike = jumps by more than 35 points and snaps back the next week (46 rows). Bed-count blip = more than 50% and at least 3 beds away from the hospital's own surrounding 9-week median (309 rows). 353 hospitals report staffed beds more than 50% away from their own overall median for 8 or more weeks, a sustained shift such as an ICU going from 12 to 4 beds. Staffed beds move with staffing, so sustained shifts are treated as real operating changes and kept. Spikes are removed from the main analysis; bed-count blips and over-100% rows are kept and tested in a sensitivity check.

what_was_done: Removed the isolated spikes from the main analysis (occupancy set to missing)
why: A one-week jump that reverses is almost always a data-entry or reporting artifact, not a real hospital filling up and emptying in 7 days.

what_was_done: Limited the analysis window to 2020-08-02 through 2024-04-21
why: Adult ICU reporting began in July 2020 and nothing valid exists before it. Window starts at the first week when at least 60% of the hospitals that ever report adult ICU data have a valid ICU occupancy value.

what_was_done: Marked hospitals with fewer than 52 valid ICU weeks as not stable reporters
why: Hospital-level rankings and tests use stable reporters only, so a hospital with two weeks of data cannot drive a result. State totals use all valid rows.

what_was_done: Joined CMS Hospital General Information on the 6-digit CMS certification number
why: 96.6% of rows matched. Unmatched rows keep their capacity data but have no county, ownership or rating.

what_was_done: Assigned each Kentucky hospital to the Lexington-side or Louisville-side by straight-line distance to a hub in each city
why: ANALYST ASSUMPTION, not the official RMOCC boundary (which I could not find). Result: {'Lexington-side': 55, 'Louisville-side': 37} Kentucky hospitals.
